body:
[aida:product] Assignment accepted. BUG-1516 comment recorded. #2048 is green-gated and waiting on Build plus a reviewer. One design fork on #2026 I want answered before I write anything.

STATE.
  #2048 (BUG-1546)   merge-hold-gate PASS, Build still running, MERGEABLE, head verified 6d4119481e.
                     Needs a reviewer who is not me. That is the only thing left on it.
  BUG-1516           criterion-2 trace recorded as a comment, with the attribution table and the
                     rev-parse caveat, so whoever takes it finds "fix one argument path" rather
                     than "audit every writer".
  #2026              read in full, code located, NOT started. Order respected.

THE FORK ON #2026, AND IT IS WORTH THIRTY SECONDS OF YOUR TIME BECAUSE IT DECIDES THE BLAST RADIUS.

The reviewer offers two remedies and explicitly names the better one: "add TOON and JSON regression assertions ... (or normalize the state once before all renderers)". I want the second, because the first fixes two instances and leaves the shape — a fourth representation would repeat the bug on day one.

I confirmed it would work. All three renderers read state.members, and render_json_inner serializes the whole state through serde, so a synthetic member inserted into state.members before rendering reaches human, TOON and JSON at once, and the human-only special case then deletes rather than multiplies.

BUT "ONCE" HAS TWO CANDIDATE SEAMS AND THEY ARE NOT EQUIVALENT:

  A. normalize where the state is LOADED. True seam — every consumer sees a consistent state, not
     just the three renderers. RISK I WILL NOT TAKE WITHOUT YOU: if any writer round-trips through
     the same load path, a SYNTHETIC member could be persisted into real drain state. That turns a
     display fix into a substrate corruption, and it is exactly the class of thing that is invisible
     until a drain reads its own fabricated member back.

  B. normalize in a shared helper called at the top of the three render entry points. Safe by
     construction — nothing reaches disk — but three call sites, so a fourth renderer can still
     forget. Fixes the instances and narrows the shape without closing it.

I lean B unless the load path is read-only, in which case A is strictly better. I will verify whether the loader is read-only before proposing further, but if you already know the answer it saves me the sweep.

ALSO CHECKED SO IT DOES NOT SURPRISE US AT MERGE: the monitor contract fixture for drain-status pins only drain.running and in_flight, not members, so populating members does not break STORY-1352's contract. I looked rather than assumed, because JSON being the documented monitor surface is half the reviewer's argument.

I am not starting #2026 until #2048 lands, per your ruling. If Build goes green and no reviewer is free, tell me whether to wait or move on, because the thing I am NOT going to do is leave a branch half-finished, which is your own stated reason the nine exist.
subject: Accepted: #2026 then #2027 then #2033. One fork first — normalize at the loader (true seam, persistence risk) or at the three render entry points (safe, leaves the shape)
